name: smtp-utf8-alabel-domain-permit-valid
description: Per RFC 9598 §3, the domain part of an SmtpUTF8Mailbox SAN MUST be in A-label form (with NR-LDH/ASCII labels lowercased). With both the rfc822Name permit and the SmtpUTF8Mailbox SAN in matching A-label form, RFC 9598 §6 requires an octet-for-octet match after lowercasing - and that's what this chain exercises.
notes: RFC 9598 obsoleted RFC 8398 and REVERSED the SmtpUTF8Mailbox domain-form rule: 8398 mandated U-labels for non-ASCII labels; 9598 mandates A-labels. 9598 §6 also dropped the A-to-U conversion during name-constraint matching, requiring direct octet-for-octet comparison after case-folding.

OpenSSL's nc_email_eai (crypto/x509/v3_ncons.c) still implements the RFC 8398 rule - it converts the rfc822 constraint from A-label to U-label via ossl_a2ulabel() and then expects the SAN domain in U-label form. The function comment still cites "RFC 8398, section 6". Against this chain (A-label/A-label) OpenSSL rejects with X509_V_ERR_PERMITTED_VIOLATION. That is a stale-spec bug, not a deliberate choice: the matching code was added in commit 69d9245996 ("RFC 8398: Name constraints validation", Aug 2019) and has not been updated for RFC 9598 (Feb 2024).
Go accepts this chain vacuously: it does not apply rfc822 name constraints to SmtpUTF8Mailbox otherName SANs at all.
Companion to `smtp-utf8-ulabel-domain-permit-valid`, which is the inverse case (U-label SAN, RFC 8398-conformant, RFC 9598-forbidden).
